text:
maya (support): Heads up — customer r-188 reports canary rollout health chart stuck at 'In progress' for ~6h. Console shows no recent events, timeline flat, but API /v1/rollouts/r-188 returns progress 0.5 and status 'in_progress'.

nina (support-lead): Escalating. Is this only r-188 or others? Any correlation to deploys/regions?

maya (support): Only r-188 so far, customer on us-west-2 dedicated. No deploys reported in last 12h. They also mentioned that clicking the rollout tile occasionally returns a 500 for the status endpoint.

deploy-bot: [deployment] status-sync v2.4.1 rolled out to redwood-status-sync namespace 3 days ago.

tj (eng-runtime): I can take a look. Can you paste the exact curl response from the API (headers + body)?

maya (support): Sure — output:

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "rollout_id":"r-188",
  "status":"in_progress",
  "progress":0.512,
  "last_event_ts": null,
  "canary_health": null
}
```

maya (support): UI shows spinner in chart and message "awaiting status updates".

eli (analytics): If last_event_ts is null that means status-sync didn't write any processed events for this rollout. Could be an ingestion/consumer gap. I'll check event ingestion metrics.

olivia (eng-sre): Quick checks I want run:
- `kubectl get pods -n redwood-status-sync`
- `kubectl logs -l app=status-sync -n redwood-status-sync --tail 200`
- `redis-cli -n 0 LLEN canary:event:queue`

olivia (eng-sre): Running now — cluster shows 2/3 status-sync pods Ready, one CrashLoopBackOff.

tj (eng-runtime): Crash logs from pod status-sync-2:

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "worker.py", line 214, in process_event
KeyError: 'health_state'
```

olivia (eng-sre): Also saw repeated warnings: `Skipped event with missing fields` and backlog count `queue_length=2436`.

eli (analytics): That backlog would explain missing last_event_ts. How long has queue been >2000?

olivia (eng-sre): Metrics show spike ~6h ago matching customer report window.

sam (product): Any recent schema changes to canary event format? We shipped a small metadata change yesterday (internal change id: CH-429) but it was supposed to be backwards compatible.

tj (eng-runtime): Looks like the worker started enforcing `health_state` presence after CH-429. If old events are missing that key we skip them and never update rollout status. That would leave UI stuck 'in_progress'.

maya (support): Customer also reported intermittent 500s when polling `/v1/rollouts/:id/status`. Could that be due to the CrashLoopBackOff pod?

olivia (eng-sre): Yes — with one pod down and long backlog the remaining pods were overloaded and sometimes timed out producing 500s.

tj (eng-runtime): Short-term mitigation: I can patch status-sync to tolerate missing `health_state` by treating it as `unknown` and continue processing. Will prepare hotfix v2.4.2.

nina (support-lead): Please communicate a timeline to the customer. They are sensitive since this is a canary for a payment change.

tj (eng-runtime): Hotfix build started. Will roll to one pod as canary, monitor queue drain.

olivia (eng-sre): Steps I'm doing now:
- scale status-sync deployment to 4 replicas
- restart CrashLoopBackOff pod
- monitor `queue_length` and `canary_event_processed`

olivia (eng-sre): Ran `kubectl scale deploy/status-sync --replicas=4 -n redwood-status-sync` — replicas increased, new pod coming up.

tj (eng-runtime): Hotfix image pushed: `redwood/status-sync:v2.4.2-hotfix` with tolerant parsing. Rolling update started.

deploy-bot: Rollout started for status-sync -> v2.4.2-hotfix (canary: pod status-sync-5)

eli (analytics): I see backlog starting to drop from 2436 -> 812 -> 210. last_event_ts for r-188 now populated (2026-03-17T10:12:07Z)

maya (support): Customer confirms chart updated and shows health transitions. They also say polling 500s stopped.

tj (eng-runtime): Root cause summary: schema enforcement introduced in CH-429 caused worker to drop older events missing new `health_state` field. Worker crash + backlog led to amplified outages and occasional 500s due to overload. Fix: tolerant parsing + ensure deployments handle schema migration (feature flag/skipping).

sam (product): Follow-ups: add a compatibility test in CI for event schema migration, and a dashboard alert when `queue_length>1000` for >5m.

nina (support-lead): Maya — please send customer update: explain cause, mitigation, and ETA for full fix and postmortem. Offer escalation credit if needed.

maya (support): Will do. Filing internal incident INC-2026-315 and a github issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/status-sync/issues/287

olivia (eng-sre): Creating runbook entry for status-sync: how to clear backlog safely, how to roll tolerant version.

tj (eng-runtime): Adding unit test for missing `health_state` and adding schema migration note to release docs.

maya (support): Thanks all — customer confirmed final state stable. Marking thread resolved after postmortem.

nina (support-lead): Great triage. Assigning owners: eng-runtime (tj) for code fix + tests; eng-sre (olivia) for runbook/alerting; analytics (eli) to add event-coverage graph; product (sam) to coordinate release notes.

maya (support): Closing from support side. :white_check_mark:
